Thanks — reviewed Acme's annotated DPA. Summary of recommended positions and possible concessions:

1) EU-US transfers: we should accept the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as the transfer mechanism and attach them as Annex A. This is the cleanest approach for enterprise customers and avoids an open-ended reliance on other mechanisms. We'll include a short representation that Redwood maintains appropriate safeguards and will execute SCCs when required.

2) Subprocessors: Acme requests 30 days' notice and an objection right with criteria. We can agree to 30 days' notice. For objection, propose: Acme may object within 30 days on reasonable grounds related to the subprocessors' access to and processing of personal data (e.g., security, lawful basis). If Acme objects, parties will meet to resolve; if unresolved, Redwood may continue if it has implemented appropriate mitigations. (We should avoid an unconditional veto.)

3) Data subject assistance: confirm standard SLA — we will cooperate and provide reasonably requested information within 30 days for routine requests; for complex requests (e.g., large-scale exports) we'll need reasonable time and may charge for extraordinary effort.

4) Subprocessor list: give them a snapshot CSV with current subprocessors and commit to updates via the privacy center URL; attach Redwood_Subprocessors_List_2026-02.csv.

5) Liability cap/indemnity redlines: flagged but not yet negotiated — advise sales to expect back-and-forth on this.

Action items:
- I'll prepare a marked-up DPA (v1) with SCC Annex and the proposed subprocessor objection language.
- Neha, please let Acme know we're prepared to add SCCs and the proposed subprocessor language, and that we'll circulate an internal mark today.

Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA - Acme initial redlines (SCCs + subprocessors)

Liam — thanks for the initial pass and for sharing the annotated DPA. We've discussed internally and can propose the following to move forward quickly: 

- Redwood will incorporate the EU Standard Contractual Clauses as an Annex to the DPA (we'll attach the text in our next version).
- We can provide 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors. For objections, we propose the following limited right: Acme may object within 30 days on reasonable grounds related to security or unlawful processing; parties will meet to try to resolve; if unresolved Redwood may continue if adequate mitigations are in place. This preserves operational flexibility while giving Acme an opportunity to review.
- Attached: Redwood's current subprocessors list and a redline of the DPA (Acme_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf).

If that sounds acceptable in principle, Monica will share the marked DPA with SCC Annex and we can aim to get the final routed to procurement for signature via DocuSign by end of day Wed (2/18).

Next steps: let us know if procurement needs the SCCs embedded (we can do either embedded or as a signed annex; embedded is faster for DocuSign).

Best,
